sections.content:
6,470 people

were counted on the census as "environmental health professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Environmental health professionals use specialist technical skills and�knowledge to protect people from health risks associated with the environment in which they live and work.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "environmental health professionals", 15.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "environmental health professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "environmental health professionals" included:

  • health services and public health managers and directors
  • managers in transport and distribution
  • education managers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "environmental health professionals" there were more women than men (58% compared with 42%).

This means "environmental health professionals" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 42% and women made up 58% of "environmental health professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "environmental health professionals" included:

  • national government administrative occupations
  • marketing and commercial managers
  • collector salespersons and credit agents

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "environmental health professionals", 11.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (80.6% compared with 19.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96.4%) than self-employed (3.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
